Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Bangladesh's reply. They have to chase down 119 runs, which is the revised target for the hosts. The Afghanistan players takes the field. Followed by Litton Das and Afif Hossain who come out for Bangladesh. It will be Fazalhaq Farooqi to start with the new ball.
... The Run Chase ...

Taskin Ahmed was sensational with his fiery spell of 3 for 33 while Mustafizur Rahman and Shakib Al Hasan chipped in with 2 apiece. Bangladesh will be the happier side going into the innings break and will be confident to chase this total. Can they do it and take the series 2-0 or will Afghan bowlers defend this? We shall find out together. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

An outstanding effort with the ball by Bangladesh keeps Afghanistan to 116 for 7 in their allotted overs. Having put into bat first, the visitors lost both the openers inside the first three overs. The ball was doing a lot initially and caused havoc for the Afghanistan batters. Mohammad Nabi and Ibrahim Zadran steadied the innings with a 32-run stand amidst the rain delay for an hour. Bangladesh pegged them back with three quick wickets and reduced the visitors to 67 for 5. Karim Janat and Azmatullah Omarzai got the innings back on track with a quick 42-run partnership. A huge hit in the final over from Rashid Khan takes Afghanistan to a respectable total.
A slower bouncer, wide outside off. Rashid Khan does not go after it as he think this is high enough for a wide. Although, the umpires think otherwise. Afghanistan end their innings at 116/7.

Update - Well, well you all know what time is it. YES! It is time for some inspection. The three umpires make their way out on the field, while doing so, that have a short chat with the Afghan skipper, Rashid Khan and on they go towards the outfield. Right then, we have a time now, the game will resume at 7.45 pm IST. Not too long now, and it has been reduced to a 17-overs match now.

Update 7.20 pm IST (1.50 pm GMT)- The umpire came out, took a stroll and are certainly unhappy with the wet outfield. The stumps have been placed, although there is no concrete news on the restart time. The wait game continues. Okay then, as expected, the umpires will conduct the next inspection at 7.35 pm IST (2.05 pm GMT).

Update 6.49 pm IST (1.29 pm GMT) - Well then, the images from the ground look quite promising, as the covers have been taken off. No signs of rain as well. OH NO! Hold your horses, some movement can be seen of the groundstaff, while the umpires can be seen guiding them. Although, still no signs of rain, that means it could be something to do with the wet outfield. Stick around for more updates.

UPDATE 6.30 pm IST (1.00 pm GMT): The rain has stopped but the covers around the pitch and the square are still in place. Let's hope the rain stays away and we get some action soon. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE 6.08 pm IST (12.38 pm GMT) - Dear, oh dear! The inevitable has happened. The ground staff is rushing towards the pitch and get the covers on in no time. The players have gone off the field. Much required breather for the Afghanistan side. The ball did all the talking so far, and now it is time to sit back and wait for the rain to passby. Hopefully, it is just a short delay.

Commentary.Commentary: The match is set to begin. Bangladesh players take the field. Followed by Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Hazratullah Zazai who walk out to open for Afghanistan. It will be Taskin Ahmed to start with the new ball.

Rashid Khan, the skipper of Afghanistan is in for a chat now. He starts by saying that it would've been great to bowl first, but hopes that the ground remains dry and focus on playing positive cricket. Mentions that the boys need to bring their experience into the game, which will help them to get over the line if the rain comes into play. Adds that it is all about the basics and it is just about adjusting to the conditions as soon as possible. Informs that they have a single change to their side.

Shakib Al Hasan, the captain of Bangladesh is in for a quick chat. He says that they will field first. Adds that they want to chase and it looks like a good wicket to bat second. Mentions that they have improved their approach and want to continue with the winning momentum. Closes by saying the two changes for them, Afif Hossain and Hasan Mahmud come in for the injured Rony Talukdar and Shoriful Islam.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Hazratullah Zazai, Ibrahim Zadran, Najibullah Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, Karim Janat, Rashid Khan (C), Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Wafadar Momand (In for Fareed Ahmad), Azmatullah Omarzai and Fazalhaq Farooqi.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (WK), Najmul Hossain Shanto, Shakib Al Hasan (C), Towhid Hridoy, Afif Hossain (In for Rony Talukdar), Shamim Hossain, Mehidy Hasan, Taskin Ahmed, Nasum Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud (In for Shoriful Islam) and Mustafizur Rahman.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of Bangladesh. They will BOWL first.

Afghanistan, on the other hand, lost wickets at regular intervals and managed to just cross the 150 mark. Nabi played a key knock of 54*off 40 while Najibullah Zadran and Azmatullah Omarzai chipped in with handy contributions. They nearly made a game out from this smallish total as Karim Janat took 3 in the final over of the chase and created panic in the Bangladesh dressing room. They however ended on the losing side. Can they bounce back and end the tour on a high? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned...

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 2nd T20I between Bangladesh and Afghanistan. After losing the ODI series, Bangladesh bounced back nicely and won the first game by 2 wickets off the penultimate ball. The Tigers kept Afghanistan at 154 with the entire blowing unit doing the job. Towhid Hridoy with 47* was the star in the chase and despite some drama in the final over, he took his side past the finish line.  Bangladesh will hope for a repeat effort and end the series on a high.
